sources.entry: evcc - Extensible Electric Vehicle Charge Controller and home energy management system. (Source Code) MIT deb/Docker/Go
evcc | EV charge controller for solar surplus charging

summary.one_liner: evcc is an extensible electric vehicle charge controller and home energy management system that aims to run locally without cloud services.
summary.what_it_does: evcc controls EV chargers and coordinates them with home energy sources such as solar inverters, battery systems, and energy meters. The README lists support for a very large set of chargers, including OCPP, EEBus, and build-your-own hardware, plus smart switches and heat pumps or electric heaters. It also integrates with many solar inverters, battery systems, and energy meters, and with vehicles for state of charge, remote charge, and preconditioning status. Generic plugins (Modbus, HTTP, MQTT, JavaScript, WebSocket, Go, shell scripts) cover devices not otherwise supported. It offers a web UI, status notifications through Telegram, PushOver and others, logging to InfluxDB and Grafana, and REST and MQTT APIs for home automation systems.
use_cases: charge an electric vehicle with surplus solar power
local home energy management without cloud services
control a wallbox or EV charger from Home Assistant or openHAB
monitor solar inverter and energy meter data
log EV charging and energy data to InfluxDB and Grafana
get charging notifications via Telegram or PushOver
how_to_run: See the documentation at docs.evcc.io for installation and getting started
Build from source as described in CONTRIBUTING.md
notable: Works locally without relying on cloud services
Very broad device support across chargers, meters, inverters, heat pumps, and vehicles
Generic plugin system (Modbus, HTTP, MQTT, JavaScript, WebSocket, shell scripts) for unsupported devices
REST and MQTT APIs for home automation integration
caveats: Some sponsor-required components are excluded from the MIT License; one sponsorship token is required per evcc instance
Home Assistant and openHAB add-ons are not maintained by the evcc core team
